\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قطعا} (qat'an)}{قطعا (qat'an)}]{\fa{قطعا} (qat'an) — definitely, certainly}

\label{lesson:FA-C393-qatan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for unlikely, then the Persian for definite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قطعا}}
\textbf{\fa{قطعا}} (\emph{qat'an}) — \textquotedblleft{}definitely, certainly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{قطعا} \fa{فردا} \fa{میآید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u qat'an fardâ miâyad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He is definitely coming tomorrow.
\end{quote}

Close to \emph{hatman} in meaning, and a little more formal.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{قطعا}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{qaṭ'an} \textquotedblleft{}decisively\textquotedblright{}, an adverb built on \emph{qaṭ'} \textquotedblleft{}cutting\textquotedblright{}, like \emph{qat'i} \textquotedblleft{}definite\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qat'an}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qat'an}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{qat'an}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for unlikely, then the Persian for definite, then say \emph{qat'an} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تردید} (tardid)}{تردید (tardid)}]{\fa{تردید} (tardid) — doubt, hesitation}

\label{lesson:FA-C393-tardid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for definite, then the Persian for definitely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تردید}}
\textbf{\fa{تردید}} (\emph{tardid}) — \textquotedblleft{}doubt, hesitation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بدون} \fa{تردید} \fa{این} \fa{بهترین} \fa{راه} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bedun-e tardid in behtarin râh ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Without doubt this is the best way.
\end{quote}

\emph{Tardid dâshtan} — to be in doubt, to hesitate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تردید}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{tardīd}, a verbal noun usually explained as going back and forth: a doubting mind wavers.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اطمینان} (etminân)}{اطمینان (etminân)}]{\fa{اطمینان} (etminân) — certainty, confidence}

\label{lesson:FA-C393-etminan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for definitely, then the Persian for doubt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اطمینان}}
\textbf{\fa{اطمینان}} (\emph{etminân}) — \textquotedblleft{}certainty, confidence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{با} \fa{اطمینان} \fa{میگویم} \fa{که} \fa{حق} \fa{با} \fa{توست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bâ etminân miguyam ke haq bâ tost.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I can say for certain that you are right.
\end{quote}

\emph{Etminân dâshtan} — to be sure; \emph{etminân dâdan} — to reassure.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اطمینان}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{iṭmi'nān} \textquotedblleft{}calm, assurance\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from the same Arabic family as \emph{muṭma'inn} \textquotedblleft{}sure\textquotedblright{}, the source of Persian \emph{motma'en}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مطمئن} \fa{شدن} (motma'en shodan)}{مطمئن شدن (motma'en shodan)}]{\fa{مطمئن} \fa{شدن} (motma'en shodan) — to make sure, to become sure}

\label{lesson:FA-C393-motmaen-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for doubt, then the Persian for certainty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مطمئن} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{مطمئن} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{motma'en shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to make sure, to become sure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{رفتن} \fa{مطمئن} \fa{شدم} \fa{که} \fa{در} \fa{قفل} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qabl az raftan motma'en shodam ke dar qofl ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Before leaving I made sure that the door was locked.
\end{quote}

\emph{Motma'en} \textquotedblleft{}sure\textquotedblright{} + \emph{shodan}. \emph{Motma'en budan} — to be sure. It is spelled with \fa{ئ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مطمئن}} comes from Arabic \emph{muṭma'inn} \textquotedblleft{}calm, sure\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); with the inherited Persian verb \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}, it means to become sure.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{motma'en shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{motma'en shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for doubt, then the Persian for certainty, then say \emph{motma'en shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ظاهرا} (zâheran)}{ظاهرا (zâheran)}]{\fa{ظاهرا} (zâheran) — apparently, seemingly}

\label{lesson:FA-C393-zaheran}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for certainty, then the Persian for to make sure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ظاهرا}}
\textbf{\fa{ظاهرا}} (\emph{zâheran}) — \textquotedblleft{}apparently, seemingly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ظاهرا} \fa{قطار} \fa{امروز} \fa{دیر} \fa{میآید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zâheran qatâr emruz dir miâyad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Apparently the train is late today.
\end{quote}

From \emph{zâher} \textquotedblleft{}outward appearance\textquotedblright{}. For what seems true from the outside.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{ظاهرا}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ẓāhiran} \textquotedblleft{}outwardly\textquotedblright{}, an adverb built on \emph{ẓāhir} \textquotedblleft{}visible, apparent\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for certainty, then the Persian for to make sure, then say \emph{zâheran} again
